name: ATR 42
sources: [F42] ATR, Factsheets: ATR 42-600 (ATR CM Marketing, June 2015), https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_42-600.pdf, the dimensions drawing (booklet p.10): overall length 22.67 m (74 ft 5 in), span 24.57 m (80 ft 7 in), wheelbase 8.78 m (28 ft 10 in), track 4.10 m, propeller axes 8.10 m apart, propeller 3.93 m, height 7.59 m, wing area 54.5 m2.

[F72] ATR, Factsheets: ATR 72-600, https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_72-600.pdf, the dimensions drawing (booklet p.22): overall length 27.166 m (89 ft 1.5 in), span 27.050 m (88 ft 9 in), wheelbase 10.77 m (35 ft 4 in), track 4.10 m, propeller axes 8.10 m, propeller 3.93 m, height 7.65 m, wing area 61 m2.

[AFM42] ATR 42-400/500 Airplane Flight Manual, section 1.03 '3 view drawing', page 1 (EASA/DGAC approved), as hosted at https://pdfcoffee.com/afm-atr-42-500-pdf-free.html: overall length 22.67 m (892.520 in), wheelbase 8.781 m (345.709 in), span 24.57 m (967.462 in), track 4.10 m, moment origin 2.362 m (92.992 in) ahead of the nose, root chord 2.574 m, reference chord (MAC) 2.285 m, moment origin to the reference chord's leading edge 11.425 m.

[AFM72] ATR 72-212A Airplane Flight Manual, section 1.03 '3 view drawing', page 1, as hosted at https://pdfcoffee.com/afm-atr-72-500-3-pdf-free.html (the same page is GEN.4 'Dimensions', page 28, of the Rev 29 manual that this work also read): overall length 27.166 m (1069.528 in), 27.149 m to the fuselage's end, wheelbase 10.772 m (424.095 in), span 27.05 m, track 4.10 m, moment origin 2.362 m ahead of the nose, root chord 2.574 m, MAC 2.303 m, moment origin to the MAC's leading edge 13.604 m.

[WBM42] ATR 42-500 Weight and Balance Manual, fleet 45, rev 1.0 (2016-09-01), as hosted at https://pdfcoffee.com/atr42-wbm-pdf-free.html: station 0 is 2.362 m ahead of the nose and the MAC's leading edge is 11.425 m from it (p.41); the tip-up centre of gravity, 63 % MAC, is at H-arm 12.865 m (p.56); attendant seats forward 7.745 m and aft 17.845 m (p.73); toilet 18.857 m (p.75). [WBM72] ATR 72-212A Weight and Balance Manual, rev 1.0 (2016-09-01), https://pdfcoffee.com/atr72-wbm-pdf-free.html: the MAC's leading edge 13.604 m from station 0 (p.41); tip-up centre of gravity, 54 % MAC, H-arm 14.848 m (p.56); attendant seats forward 7.75 m and aft 22.341 m (p.75); toilet 23.353 m (p.77). H-arm is metres aft of station 0.

[SB72] ATR 72-200/-210 brochure, https://skybrary.aero/sites/default/files/bookshelf/3697.pdf: 'derived from the ATR 42 with a 4.5 m stretched fuselage', the same cross section and the same cockpit. [SB42] ATR 42-600 brochure (ATR CM Marketing, June 2015), https://skybrary.aero/sites/default/files/bookshelf/3695.pdf, page 2: the same dimensions as [F42] (22.67 m, 8.78 m, 24.57 m, 7.59 m, 8.10 m, 3.93 m, 4.10 m, 54.5 m2) and, in its text, high commonality with the ATR 72-600.

Total length. The overall lengths differ by 27.166 - 22.67 = 4.496 m. foreM + aftM = -1.99 - 2.51 = -4.50 m: 4 mm more, inside the 5 cm. The base mesh is 27.15 m long, so the model comes out at 22.65 m.

foreM, ahead of the wing: -1.99 m. The nose gear rides on the nose section and the mains on the wing, so the wheelbase difference is the plug ahead of the wing: 10.772 - 8.781 = 1.991 m [AFM72, AFM42]; the factsheets give 10.77 - 8.78 = 1.99 m [F72, F42]. Check: the tip-up centre of gravity stands on the main wheels, H-arm 12.865 m (42) and 14.848 m (72) [WBM42, WBM72], so the main gear is 10.503 m and 12.486 m aft of the nose (station 0 is 2.362 m ahead of it) and moves 1.983 m (the percentages are whole numbers: +-0.02 m); the nose gear is then 10.503 - 8.781 = 1.722 m and 12.486 - 10.772 = 1.714 m aft of the nose, the same in both, so the whole difference is between the nose gear and the wing. Measured on the two factsheet side drawings (the nose and the tail from the length dimension's end lines): the propeller disc is 6.88 m and 8.92 m aft of the nose, 2.04 m apart; the forward door (4.25 m) and the cockpit are at the same place. Not used: the MAC's leading edge, 11.425 m and 13.604 m from station 0, moves 2.179 m; the MACs differ (2.285 and 2.303 m) because the outer wings differ, so the MAC's leading edge is not the same station of the common inner wing (the root chord is 2.574 m on both). The draft of this recipe used -2.19 from it: the wheelbase it gives (8.58 m) is 0.2 m short of the published 8.78 m.

aftM, behind the wing: -2.51 m = -4.496 + 1.99 (what is left of the length difference). Check: everything behind the wing moves by the whole 4.496 m: the aft attendant seat 22.341 - 17.845 = 4.496 m and the toilet 23.353 - 18.857 = 4.496 m [WBM72, WBM42], while the forward attendant seat does not move (7.75 and 7.745 m). The aft passenger door's centre line on the two factsheet drawings is 15.35 m and 19.71 m aft of the nose, 4.36 m apart (the drawings are schematic, 3 %): it is behind both plugs. No document prints the plugs or the frame stations as such; the split is derived from the gear, the datum and the length.

Doors and cockpit [F42, F72, WBM42, WBM72]: the same doors on both (the entrance door aft on the left, the cargo door forward on the left, the service door aft on the right: the factsheets' left side drawings and the WBMs' cabin layouts), the same nose and cockpit [SB72]. No door is added or left out, and the entrance door is behind both plugs, so no 'stations' entry: the base's door (19.7 m, from the ATR 72-600 brochure https://skybrary.aero/sites/default/files/bookshelf/3696.pdf) moves with the fuselage, by the tool, to 15.2 m: 7.47 m from the tail, as on the ATR 72.

Gear: the same layout on both: two wheels on each main leg and two on the nose leg, track 4.10 m, the mains in the nacelles ([SB42] page 2, front view; [AFM72] GEN.4 front view of the Rev 29 manual); the track is 4.10 m in [F42], [F72], [AFM42] and [AFM72]. Only the wheelbase differs (above), which the tool takes from foreM, so no 'gear' entry. No ATR document that this work had prints the tyre sizes, so whether the ATR 42's tyres differ from the ATR 72's is not known here: the base's are kept. Note on the base: its gear entry puts the nose gear 2.9 m aft of the nose, but the published station is 1.71 m ([WBM72] tip-up 12.486 m minus the wheelbase 10.772 m; [F72] drawing 1.70 m), and the mains 13.67 m aft of the nose against 12.49 m: the wheelbase is right, both legs are 1.2 m too far aft, and this model inherits that.

Nacelles: the same on both: propeller axes 8.10 m apart, propeller 3.93 m (Hamilton Standard 568F-1 on the ATR 42-500 and the ATR 72-212A in EASA TCDS A084, issue 14, 2026-02-23, https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/downloads/7358/en), and the engines are the PW127 family [F42, F72]; no 'nacelle' entry. The older ATR 42-300 (AT43) has 3.6 m four-blade propellers (PW120); the model shows the 42-500/-600.

Wingtip: none on either aircraft (neither has a winglet, no 'wingtip' entry). THE WING IS NOT SHORTENED: the ATR 42's span is 24.57 m against the ATR 72's 27.05 m [F42, F72], 2.48 m less (the ATR 42's outer wing panels are shorter, and its wing area 54.5 m2 against 61 m2), and the tool keeps the base's wing, so this model's wing is 27.05 m across, 10 % too wide. The root chord and the nacelles are common (2.574 m, 8.10 m), so the error is in the outer panels only. The model's box and the lights outboard (the navigation lights) stay on the 27.05 m span.
